institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to try to study in a place with more nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had the most amazing semester.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult and frustrating in the beginning. The process of finding out which courses i could take, took a long time and there was a lot of paperwork. However once i arrived it was very easy, and there was a lot of information in the first week.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were an introduction week for international students, where all the information was given.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There orientation week was good and provided a lot of information. However the universitys erasmus coordinater had super long answering times on mail, and often didnt even answer the question. A lot of people had this experience. However i found the help i needed through other counslers at the university, this was a little complicated to find.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There is an organisation called Samskipnaden that has cheap student housing, however a lot of people apply for their places, and there is not enough for everyone. I applied in march and didnt get a place. Instead i ended up renting a room through the privat housing website hybel. It ended up being really nice, however it was very stressful since i only got the place 3 weeks before my arrival. Some of the people that did get a place through samskipnaden told me that they applied in January og even earlier, even before they were accepted by the university, and before they were told that they could apply. My advise is to look a long time before, there is a lot of turists in Tromsø, which means that it is not that easy for students to find affordable housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Tromsø is not that big so there is no living places on campus. There is the student organisation Samskipnaden that offers some student housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I visited some of my friends that lived at samskipnadens housing, and i think they were pretty nice for the price.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it was pretty easy once i arrived.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration proces was quite simple once we arrived. In the orientation week they gave all the information needed, and they signed the proof of attendance form, this paper however needs to be printed before.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The erasmus coordinater was avialible, but there were really long answering times. However the university has a lot of other counslers at the different faculties, it was a bit difficult to find their contact information however they were super helpfull and answered way faster.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start on all the paperwork as soon as you can, take one thing at a time, and remember it will all be worth it when you arrive!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked the courses, and i liked that there was a way more chill vibe at the university then at KU.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3 bachelors courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a bit different. It was small classes, with around 5-25 students at the lectures and there was not as much practical work with assignments that i am used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Generell og marin bioteknologi
Arctic Norway aspects of culture
Bioinformatics an introduction

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The course in bioinformatics was a course i had to take. It was pretty similar to the courses at KU however a bit easier. The course in Generell og marin bioteknologi was mostly about working with articles. Some of the lectures were interesting but it was a lot of different topics, and we didnt really get into depth with any of them. The professor also told os that the course is more ment as an inspirational course. it was a very easy course and the easiest exam i have ever been to, which was very nice, however i was a bit disapointed that there was not that much related to the marine. The course in arctic Norway was very spacy and very different from any other course i have had since it is also a antropology course, a lot of exchange students takes this course which was nice.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I ended up spending a lot more money on trips than i imagened. I went on a trip to Svalbard which was amazing but also expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food was not as expensive as expected. It was a lot like the danish prices, however vegetables were more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is an organisation calles TSI, that has all the different kind of sports you would want to to, this is pretty cheap. Also Kraft Sportscenter has a lot of good opertunities. Furtheremore there was a very nice knitting club. There were so many nice activities that is was almost difficult to choose. I was a part of TSI climbing, kayaking and fjellgruppe.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definetly recommend to sign up to some of the sports and especially the outdoor once if you like that, since the nature is amazing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to go to Lofoten, we rented a car and brought tents and stayed there for 5 days, it was amazing! also i would recommend to get a membership at DNT, then you will be able to get a key that works to all the different huts in the area. Also i would recommend sommerøya, really an amazing place.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy since it is very much like the danish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up to some of the sports! also i shared an apartment with a Norwegian girl which made it a lot easier to get Norwegian friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really loved that everyone liked the outdoors. Everyone wanted to go hiking, kayaking, fishing and more which was amazing. Also i liked that everyone seemed a bit more chill than in copenhagen, no one seemed to be as busy.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I would say that it is the most amazing place if you like the outdoors and like mountains. However if you are more of a city person i would maybe choose another place, since the town is cozy but very small and it would probably get a bit boring if you dont like nature.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to take vitamin D in the winter.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends i made and the experiences. I loved everything and i think it was the best months of my life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to study for the exams as it got darker. When the sun went down at 1 pm i got so tired and it was difficult to stay motivated to study. However it helped to do it with friends, and also to go outside.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
